title: What is nitrous oxide (laughing gas) and what are its effects?
intro: Nitrous oxide, known as laughing gas, is a colourless gas used in medicine and dentistry to reduce pain and anxiety. It is also misused as a recreational drug, which carries real health risks. Used correctly in medical settings it is generally safe.

sections.heading: Medical use
paragraphs: Mixed with oxygen, usually in a half-and-half mixture, it is inhaled through a mask. It is used in dental procedures, during childbirth and for minor procedures in children. It has a quick effect, wears off within minutes after the mask is removed and usually allows people to drive soon after, as advised by staff.

sections.heading: Effects
paragraphs: It produces a feeling of relaxation, light-headedness, tingling and sometimes laughter or a floating feeling, along with reduced pain and anxiety. Side effects include nausea, dizziness, headache and sleepiness. In high concentrations it can cause confusion, and it should not be used by some people, such as those with certain lung conditions or in early pregnancy without advice.

sections.heading: Recreational use and dangers
paragraphs: Misuse involves inhaling gas from cartridges or balloons for a short high. Dangers include falls and injuries, lack of oxygen, loss of consciousness and frostbite of the lips and throat from cold gas. Regular or heavy use can destroy vitamin B12, causing numbness, tingling, weakness, difficulty walking and spinal cord damage, which can be permanent. Mixing with alcohol increases the risk.

sections.heading: Getting help
paragraphs: Seek medical advice if you have tingling, numbness, weakness or balance problems after using nitrous oxide. Stopping use and treatment with vitamin B12 may help. Support services can help with substance use. In many countries, the sale of the gas for inhalation is restricted.

sections.heading: Safe practice
paragraphs: Use only under medical supervision for pain relief. Do not drive after misuse, and never use it alone or while standing. Environmental effects are another concern, because it is a greenhouse gas.

examples.title: Using it at the dentist
examples.text: Imagine you are afraid of dental treatment. You could ask the dentist whether nitrous oxide sedation is an option for you.

examples.title: Recognising a warning sign
examples.text: Suppose a friend who often inhales it reports numb feet. You might encourage a medical check, since vitamin B12 damage can be serious.
